results.fact: Total gain: gain_ft vs. itinerary total
results.correct_value: about 5,500 ft car to car (day 1 ~3,300 ft gain / ~600 ft loss; day 2 ~2,200 ft gain incl. the ~1,500 ft summit climb and the re-climb to Cache Col)
results.evidence: A GPS-track route page gives 5.5 mi and 3,307 ft of gain from the Cascade Pass trailhead to Kool-Aid Lake; a trip report gives ~3,550 ft of gain from the trailhead to Cache Col. Both the stored 1,700 ft and the itinerary's 4,800 ft are below what the row's own waypoints demand (TH 3,600 -> Cache Col 6,903 -> lake 6,200 -> summit 7,821 -> col -> TH is >= 5,600 ft).

results.fact: Day-2 (summit + hike out) duration vs. its own schedule
results.correct_value: a ~9-hour day: summit round trip ~3.5 h from 4:30 AM, start the hike out ~8:30 AM, trailhead ~1:30 PM
results.evidence: The day's hours (9), timing.summitTimeHrs (9), the sectionBreakdown (9) and totalHrs (14.5 = 5.5 + 9) all agree on 9 h; the schedule's own relative steps put the party back at camp ~8:00 AM and the day note says 'back at camp by mid-morning', so only the 12:00 PM / ~5:00 PM clock times (a 4-hour idle gap) are the outlier. A trip report gives ~3.2 h for the camp-summit-camp round trip, consistent with the schedule's 3.5 h.

results.fact: total trip gain/loss vs itinerary day sums
results.correct_value: 11,500 ft gain and loss in total (gain_ft/loss_ft already correct); days re-split to 5,900/1,800, 3,400/3,400, 2,200/6,300
results.evidence: A trip report on this exact approach (Canyon Creek, Jerry Glacier, Crater Creek Meadows camp) gives ~22 mi with 11,500 ft gained and lost; a separate 3-day South Face ascent logged 11,558 ft over 24.5 mi. So gain_ft/loss_ft (11,500) are right and the day values (summing to 9,500/9,400) are low. The row's own pins require day 1 to climb >= 5,560 ft (TH 1,900 -> fork 5,260 -> Crater Lake 5,000 -> saddle 7,200) and lose >= 1,460 ft to the 6,000 ft camp; day 3 is its reverse. The new split keeps each day's net change (+4,100 / 0 / -4,100) and sums to 11,500 both ways.
